title: Mark the reasoning, not the outcome
statement: Mark a prediction on whether the learner used the idea, not on whether it comes true.
detail: The closing-questions design's third question has no answer key by design: a child who applies the idea has succeeded even if the next part of the story goes differently (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-closing-questions-2026-09-24/Closing_Questions_Pattern.txt`). It takes the question out of the answer-checker entirely, since there is nothing to match against.

evidence.quote: There is no answer key, and there should not be one.
Mark on whether the rule was used, not on whether the prediction turns out right.
**Q3 marking.** The document says both "mark on whether the rule was used" and "removes the question from the answer-checker entirely". The design follows the second.
No right answer here. It is marked on whether you use the idea.
